moments.title: Hi. 😊 Swedish dude here again. When we have kids. we get 480 paid parental leave days. Per child. 390 days at ~80% of pay. 90 days at a low flat rate. Separate from my 25 paid vacation days. Separate from the 120 days of
moments.selftext: Hi. 😊 Swedish dude here again. When we have kids. we get 480 paid parental leave days. Per child. 390 days at ~80% of pay. 90 days at a low flat rate. Separate from my 25 paid vacation days. Separate from the 120 days of potential sick-child days. 90 days per parent are locked to that parent and cannot be transferred. Single parent: the full 480 days. Usable until the child is 12. By law. Both of us can even stay home at the same time for 60 of those days in the first year. Together. Follow for more glimpses into life in a social democracy, where dignity is not a privilege. Peace ✌🏼 ps. this is my series on Sweden & social democracy 🇸🇪

moments.selftext: “If you want to destroy any nation without war, make nudity or adultery common in the younger generation.” - Salahuddin Ayyubi Salahuddin Ayyubi, widely known as Saladin, founded the Ayyubid dynasty and became one of the most celebrated Muslim military leaders in history. Best remembered for reclaiming Jerusalem in 1187, he earned lasting respect for his leadership, strategic skill, chivalry, and strong sense of moral discipline. This reflection suggests that a civilization’s greatest strength comes from its values rather than its military might. When moral standards weaken among younger generations, discipline and unity begin to fade. Societies may ultimately fall from internal decline when they lose the principles and character needed to preserve and protect themselves.

moments.selftext: OpenAI researcher on what has all the lab employees suddenly scared: >"SSI’s rumored result that they have cracked “test-time training,” creating a new scaling law." >"models hack external websites to keep themselves 'alive'." >"there is a large gap between the internal and external perception of the rate of progress" >"If all of this is allowed to go unchecked, we would likely have rapid runaway capability takeoff very soon, with misaligned models that hack whatever they can to get what they want" >"From an internal perspective, this might look like sitting inside Anthropic with the new Mythos 5, seeing all of the new insane things it can do (like hack into xyz website that was thought to be secure), and then you look over at your plots and see that you’ve barely scratched the surface of 2 new scaling laws and 1 existing one. And you have WAY more room to go. Then you think “holy shit this stuff is going to get so much better very very soon.”"
